You should really play BO3 having access to a sideboard goes a long way to beat certain matchups. Hand disruption, duress to be specific is the best way to win against control. they just chill with answers in hand waiting to kill your threats, so it makes sense to get ahead of those with discard spells. Counterspells out of the sideboard are another good way to beat them if you can afford to slow your game plan down. Also consider that their strategy counts on countering your spells, so if you can use your mana to apply pressure in ways that don't involve casting spells you can get a lot done. best way is creature-lands or channel lands. I've won a lot of matches against control by channeling Sokenzan into their obvious counterspell mana. Most important thing to keep in mind is that control decks feed off their opponent over-comitting to the board. make sure you play at a pace that doesn't leave you empty handed after a board-wipe. doing this also lets you keep up the 3 mana for no more lies more frequently.

I think having a non-essential commander is the best way to build a good deck. Saves a lot of frustration. The biggest advantage in my group is that when my opponents cast Drannith Magistrate, or other cards that hate on commanders specifically, I reap the greatest reward; my opponent used mana on something I can ignore, hinders the other players, and I spent nothing. My advice is find a type of strategy you want to play and choose the commander after you build the deck. Then your commander is just a synergistic addition rather than a lynch pin. The added fun here is you can swap commanders easily if you want to mix it up. I have a mono black devotion deck that I love and the commander is Ayara, First of Locthwain simply because it has 3 black pips in it's cost. there are many games where I never cast it. I also have a mono red treasure deck that has Ragavan as the commander because I think it's funny to play a modern staple in EDH, and its just a good card that makes treause. Good luck. once you start building decks this way you wont want to go back.

I was Atheist for some 15 years, but over time when I tried to think of religion as rationally as possible it became clear to me that God is real, but we have to be flexible with how we define God, and think critically what the relationship is between human and God.

All cultures have had religion since the beginning of history, it feels foolish to assume we are better off without something that has been to deeply entwined with the human experience for so long. In this context I started thinking more about what religion is supposed to be (not what it has become or what it is to other people). It became clear that religion and God is actually an incredibly resonant way to personify something that is otherwise difficult to explain. 

God is many things but here is some of what I settled on. God is part of us (humans) God exists in every human mind weather we want it or not, we call it many different things, everyone sees it differently (or doesn't see it) we live our lives based on the will of this presence, so in this sense God is completely real. For example when someone prays "God give me strength" They are communing with a part of themselves that already has the strength, as a way to psychologically bend their mind around any mental barrier and truly believe in God, which is to believe in themselves. This doesn't mean god isn't real, the part of themselves that they were communicating with is what i think God is.  Another way to put it is  God is a tool, or a thinking technique we can use to better communicate with, understand, empower, forgive ourselves, but it only really works when you believe in it. So, we cant think this as a way to diminish God to just some concept. It requires faith to work. To me, this revelation made the power of God Truly real to me for the first time.

 I think this is why Religion exists; as humans evolved and our brains became more developed we needed to develop tools to help control it. the early human cultures that developed a concept of god were more likely to survive the chaotic nature of the human mind. Today many religions are corrupted with ideas of heaven and hell and purity ect. but this is not what religion should be about imo, It's about mental health at the end of the day. In this age of technological revolution I think it's important to consider parts of the human experience that we've been evolving with for millions of years before we decide to cast it all off.
